Issuance: Notice on Reporting of Fraud Incidents (BU/N-3/2022/74)
Scope:
All banks in Brunei Darussalam licensed under  Banking Order, 2006;

All licensed, registered, or regulated financial institutions  and approved operators of payment systems that have been approved to operate in BruneiDarussalam
Detailed requirements (EN): •	Notice on Reporting of Fraud Incidents : Banks must establish their own fraud policy approved by their respective Board of Directors. The policy should define the classification of fraud incidents (material or non-material). Banks shall also notify BDCB within 1 working day upon detection of suspected material fraud, submit report within 5 working days, and provide resolution summary within 10 working days.
Primary fraud controls: Incident reporting timelines; governance policies; technology risk controls; cyber intrusion detection; IT Incident Categorization
Customer/user protection: In exercising its powers in relation to payment systems under the Oversight Act, the BDCB shall have regard to the interests of the public, and in this respect, the Authority may take into consideration — (a) whether any payment system is, in the opinion of the Authority — (i) financially safe for use by participants; (ii) efficient; and (iii) not materially causing or contributing to increased risk to the financial system; and (b) such other matters as the Authority may consider to be relevant.
Incident reporting: Banks to notify BDCB within 1 working day upon detection of suspected material fraud, submit report within 5 working days, and provide resolution summary within 10 working days
Prescribed reporting template?: Yes, as provided under Appendix 1 & Schedule 2 of the BDCB's Notice on Reporting of Fraud Incidents
Contents of reporting template:
Date and time incident was discovered.
Type of fraud incident.
Optional fields: Possible root cause; Possible impact;
Possible actions to be taken.

Resolution Summary

Duration to resolve the incident.
Actions taken to resolve the incident.
Enforcement actions for non-compliance: Administrative penalties, directives, suspension/revocation (Oversight Act).

Issuance: Prakas on Systemic Risk Management of Payment System (B9-06-235);
Scope: All banks, Microfinance Institutions, insurers, capital market firms, and other licensed financial institutions, all regulated by NBC, CAFIU, and MEF.
Detailed requirements (EN):
•	Mandatory verification of customer identity.
•	Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO): Identify and verify the true owners of accounts or companies.
•	Enhanced due diligence for government officials, their families, and associates.
•	Customers must be classified into risk levels (low, medium, high) based on activity and background.
•	Systems must detect unusual or suspicious transactions.
•	Automated alerts for large or unusual transfers.
•	Extra scrutiny for international transactions to prevent money laundering and fraud.
•	PSPs must implement secure systems to prevent hacking and unauthorized access.
•	Backup and recovery plans to prevent fraud during outages.
•	Mandatory reporting to NBC’s Financial Intelligence Unit.
•	Continuous review of customer activity.
•	PSPs must provide clear channels for fraud complaints.
•	Customer funds must be segregated and protected from misuse.
Primary fraud controls: Led by the Cambodia Financial Intelligence Unit (CAFIU) and supported by industry initiatives (ABC) and international AML/CFT standards. CAFIU collects, analyzes, and disseminates Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) from banks, insurers, and other financial institutions and coordinates with international bodies like the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) and Financial Action Task Force (FATF).
Customer/user protection: The system relies on KYC, transaction monitoring, suspicious activity reporting, and regulatory inspections to combat fraud across banks, MFIs, insurers, and payment providers.
Authentication/tech:
•	Mandatory identity verification for opening bank accounts, mobile wallets, and insurance policies.
•	Requires national ID, passport, or business registration documents.
•	Fingerprint and facial recognition 
•	Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) combines password/PIN + SMS OTP (one-time password) or app-based token.
•	Real-time monitoring of unusual or suspicious activity.
Incident reporting:
Incident reporting is sector-specific: CamCERT for cybersecurity and CAFIU for financial fraud. Reporting channels include online forms, emails, phone hotlines, and structured databases, all designed to strengthen transparency, security, and compliance.

CAIFU requires Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) from banks, insurers, and payment service providers. Covered institutions are required to report fraud, money laundering, or unusual financial activity.
Prescribed reporting template?: NBC requires banks and financial institutions to use standardized reporting templates, prescribed under its Prakas (regulations), for financial, prudential, and compliance reporting.
Contents of reporting template:
•	Balance Sheet 
o	Assets (cash, deposits, loans, investments)
o	Liabilities (deposits, borrowings, payables)
o	Equity (capital, reserves, retained earnings)
•	Income Statement 
o	Interest income and expenses
o	Non-interest income (fees, commissions)
o	Operating expenses
o	Net profit/loss
•	Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR)
•	Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR)
•	Loan-to-Deposit Ratio (LDR)
•	Large Exposure Limits (concentration risk reporting)
•	Loan classification (standard, substandard, doubtful, loss)
•	Provisioning requirements
•	Sectoral distribution of loans (agriculture, trade, services, etc.)
•	Non-performing loans (NPLs) and recovery actions
•	Foreign exchange exposure
•	Interest rate risk
•	Operational risk events
•	Anti-Money Laundering (AML) compliance reporting
•	Loan portfolio by client type (individual, group, SME)
•	Average loan size
•	Client outreach (number of borrowers, geographic distribution)
•	Social performance indicators (if required by NBC)
Enforcement actions for non-compliance: Revocation, fines, or suspension under NBC Prakas authority.

Issuance: Payment Systems Act B.E. 2560
Scope: Financial institutions; Highly Important Payment Systems; Designated Payment Systems; Designated Payment Services
Detailed requirements (EN):
Payment service providers must adopt board-approved IT security and fraud risk management policies covering access control, confidentiality, integrity, availability, incident response, and audit. Annual independent IT security audits are required, with results submitted to BOT. In 2023, BOT mandated additional sector-wide anti-fraud measures, including restrictions on communication channels, strengthened authentication, transaction monitoring, and coordinated fraud response mechanisms.

Furthermore, the 2025 draft guidlines requires Payment Service Providers to implement end-to-end digital fraud management frameworks. These include the adoption of board-approved policies and KPIs covering the full fraud lifecycle, from prevention and monitoring to detection, response, and customer remediation.
Primary fraud controls:
Preventive, detective, and responsive controls; Mandatory transaction monitoring; Restrictions on phishing vectors; Ability to suspend or freeze suspicious transactions; Coordination with AML authorities.

Providers are required to implement risk-based customer due diligence (CDD), continuously monitor transactions for suspicious behavior, and apply appropriate authentication measures depending on transaction risk and service channels.
Customer/user protection: Mandatory customer alerts and transaction notifications; 24/7 fraud hotlines; Measures to prevent unauthorized transactions and support timely remediation.
Authentication/tech: Biometrics for high-value transfers or limit changes; monitoring tech
Incident reporting: Mandatory incident recording and reporting to BOT through supervisory channels; Timely notification and post-incident reporting required.
Prescribed reporting template?: No
Contents of reporting template: Regulation does not prescribe a single public template; Supervisory reporting typically includes incident type, detection date, affected systems, customer impact, root cause, remedial actions, and control enhancements.
Enforcement actions for non-compliance: Fines, corrective orders, suspension by BOT.

Issuance: Circular No. 35/2016/TT-NHNN on safety and confidentiality of internet banking
Scope: Credit institutions, foreign bank branches, intermediary payment service providers
Detailed requirements (EN): Circular 35 sets technical and administrative measures for secure internet and mobile banking, including transaction confirmation methods, monitoring, confidentiality, vulnerability management and customer guidance. Decision 2345 mandates biometric authentication for high-value online transfers, device change alerts, notification, and limits for card payments; SBV issued  guidance 5262 for varying ID scenarios and NFC limitations.
Primary fraud controls: Strong authentication, transaction categorisation, monitoring, alerts, limits
Customer/user protection: Enhanced authentication shielding customers for high-value transactions
Authentication/tech: Biometric or electronic ID matching; OTP; NFC/chip ID card integration
Incident reporting: Storage of device and authentication logs; operational guidance
Prescribed reporting template?: Yes (SBV circulars specify formats).
Contents of reporting template: Institution details, incident nature, authentication failure, financial impact, remedial actions.
Enforcement actions for non-compliance: Fines, suspension, license revocation by SBV.
